fact: Nigeria Customs Service Comptroller-General Adewale Adeniyi says it has deployed AI-enabled scanners that guide image analysts to predict the nature of imported items.

The Nigeria Customs Service says it uses AI in some processes, including an AI/machine-learning Smart Fraud Detection model in NICIS that helps officers assess declaration risk, an AI HS-code search and an AI vehicle valuation system.
The report relayed by Nairametrics says AI is being applied in Nigerian social welfare programmes to map urban poverty.

fact: Minister of State for Health Iziaq Salako said the National Centre for Artificial Intelligence and Robotics under NITDA is leading projects to integrate AI into healthcare delivery.
The review reports AI-powered traffic management pilots in Lagos and Abuja that have reportedly reduced peak-hour travel times by 20%.

Punch reports the Presidency's National Agro-Productivity System, an AI platform using machine learning to classify land cover and identify crops on each farm parcel, began a pilot in 59 Jigawa communities in November 2026.

Nigeria signed an MoU on 17 July 2026 to launch NAPS, an agricultural monitoring platform whose AI algorithms identify farmland and crops from satellite images, to be deployed gradually starting with a one-state pilot.

NASRDA said farmers in seven demonstration states would be supported with AI-based tools for data collection and analysis, and the project's expert said the planned information system would include voice-based AI advisory services.

The Nigeria Customs Service told the WTO Trade Facilitation Committee that its B'Odogwu system integrates AI-enabled risk analytics, with four live AI application areas across the clearance chain including HS code prediction, valuation benchmarking and predictive selectivity.
